objections.gloss: Criminalizing assistance and presence does not prevent the sovereign exit — it manufactures the solitary, more violent death its proponents lament, and the obstruction is wrong on sovereignty before…
objections.title: Assisting or even being present at a suicide should be a crime — it deters, and it refuses complicity in a grave act.

objections.gloss: The objection treats coerced deaths under a permissive regime as decisive while ignoring that prohibition neither eliminates coercion nor escapes the symmetric error of forcing the freely-decided to…
objections.title: Permit it and the option becomes a weapon against the weak — the elderly and disabled pressured, made to feel a burden, eased toward a door they never wanted; open it and you license atrocity, so it must stay shut for everyone.

objections.gloss: The objection vaults from 'this condition can impair some decisions' to 'this person can validly decide nothing about their own life' — an overgeneralization capacity assessment is built to refuse…
objections.title: You can't give valid consent to dying when you're mentally ill — the illness is making the choice, so honoring it isn't respecting autonomy, it's abandoning someone to their disorder.

objections.gloss: The objection treats palliation as a substitute for permission — assuming the request is exhaustively a demand for pain relief, so any relief a clinician can supply renders it moot — when…
objections.title: Good palliative and hospice care can control suffering to the very end — terminal sedation reaches even the cases nothing else does. So no one truly *needs* assisted death; they are driven to it by gaps in care. Fund palliation properly and the demand dissolves. Permitting death just lets us avoid fixing what is actually broken.

objections.gloss: The argument leaps from 'life has (sacred) value' to 'others may forcibly preserve this life against its bearer' — a license that only follows if the sanctity binds the agent without their consent…
objections.title: Life is sacred and inviolable — ending it is wrong whatever the person wants, and society may step in to honor that inviolability.

objections.gloss: The charge conflates a debt owed to others with a license for others to forcibly hold the body — but a debt grounds a claim against the agent, never the right to imprison them.
objections.title: Suicide is selfish — it dumps unbearable pain on the people left behind, who never consented to that grief.

objections.gloss: The slogan smuggles a universal ('all such problems are temporary') that is empirically false for intractable cases, and even where reversibility is uncertain it conflates the authority to choose…
objections.title: Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem — whatever's driving it will pass, and then the irreversible choice is made on a feeling that would have lifted.
